notes: Mission BOM for the MissionPCB demo. Kept separate from seed-parts.json,
which is the generic library; this file is the parts list for one product.
Clearance fields are intentionally written in two different styles here
(property-keyed and category-keyed) because the loader normalizes both.
Dimensions are representative package sizes, not verified against a
specific manufacturer drawing. Confirm against datasheets before layout.

parts.name: ECG Analog Front End (24-bit, single lead)
parts.placement_notes: Keep electrode traces to this part short, symmetric, and guarded. This is the most noise-critical part on the board: the input signal is roughly 1 mV.

parts.name: BLE System-on-Chip (Cortex-M4F)
parts.placement_notes: Digital switching and the radio PA both live here. Keep it on the digital side of the board, away from the analog front end.

parts.name: 2.4 GHz Chip Antenna
parts.placement_notes: Mount at a board edge with the keep-out facing open space. No copper pour, no ground plane, and no bulk material inside the keep-out.

parts.name: Buck Regulator 3.3 V (with inductor)
parts.placement_notes: The 10 mm thermal radius covers heat spreading through the copper pour, not just the package body. Switching node is the dominant EMI source on this board.

parts.name: LiPo Pouch Cell 150 mAh
parts.placement_notes: Dominates the height budget and the board area. Keep it away from sustained heat; a sealed shell gives the cell nowhere to dump energy.

parts.name: Pogo Charge Pads (4-pin)
parts.placement_notes: Must register with the gasketed charge window. The patch is sealed, so this is the only external interface after assembly.

parts.name: Ag/AgCl Electrode Snap Pad
parts.placement_notes: Pressed against the patient for the wear duration. Two are required to form the lead vector, and they must sit at opposite ends of the long axis.
